stage1.impression: A long, warm, brown room with a convincing overall layout and believable perspective, but at 1:1 it reads as a soft CG proof: the walls are a blotchy sponge texture rather than board-formed concrete, the floor and bar front are smeared by the denoiser, and the front-left quarter is a near-black void. The eye is pulled to an over-bright, washed-out cream listening room at the back, where the Ember speakers are small salmon-pink shapes half hidden behind identical lounge chairs, so the hero does not read at a glance and the frosted hand screen reads as a flat poster.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker must read at a glance as a saturated red, back-lit acrylic object: in the far room it is currently salmon (r 224, g 169, b 159), about 20 x 40 px of a 720 px frame, and half blocked by chairs
The listening room must not be the brightest thing in the frame: region [280,172,442,300] has median 160 against a frame median of 27, which flattens the far end into a cream lightbox
The walls must read as board-formed concrete (board lines, tie holes, pour lines) at 1:1, not mottled stucco
The foreground bar and stools must hold detail: [0,300,300,480] median is 9.3, so the bar front, stools and floor are unreadable
No denoiser smear on the floor, stools or wall: render at full size with enough samples
The frosted screens must glow like back-lit frosted acrylic, softly diffusing the image, not like a printed poster
The acrylic program (clear back-bar shelves with glowing edges, the Fog pair in their niches, the smoked partition) is mostly invisible and must read
Some sign of life in the foreground (a coat, a record out of its sleeve, a half-full glass catching light)

defects.what: Listening room over-exposed and low contrast, a cream lightbox (median 160, p95 236) that steals the frame
Left Ember reads as a pale pink chair back, not a red tinted acrylic horn; desaturated (r 224, g 169, b 159)
Right Ember is the same, and partly hidden behind a lounge chair
Four identical lounge chairs in a row with identical reading-light squares, obviously one model repeated, blocking the speakers
Foreground bar front and stools almost black (median 9.3, range 15), shapes are only just made out
Concrete wall is blotchy mottled noise like sponge-painted plaster, with no board grain, tie holes or pour lines
Frosted screen reads as a flat grey-white poster with a printed image, with no glowing frosted depth or edge glow
Floor reflection smeared and soft, with denoiser blotches; reads as a waxy CG surface
Back-bar: clear acrylic shelves and lit edges barely register; the niches with the Fog speakers are not legible
Front pendant is a flat white cylinder with 2.3 % clipped and no internal gradation; reads as a CG primitive
Ceiling and fir beams flat and veiled by haze (range 23.5); no checks or end grain visible
No smoked acrylic partition reads between the bar and the listening room; the opening looks empty
Proof at 0.3 scale: everything is soft; small props (glasses, menus) are smudges

changes.problem: The listening room is a blown cream lightbox that is six times brighter than the room and pulls the eye away from the speaker.

evidence.measured: lum_median 159.9, p95 235.5, against a frame median of 27.4; inner wall [330,185,410,245] median 163

change.setting: record-wall strip emission; record wall spots
change.from: strip 1.0; 3 x spot 13.5 W, cone 60 deg
change.to: strip 0.35; 3 x spot 6 W, cone 35 deg, aimed at the records only so the white wall falls off

changes.expected: The far room drops to a warm mid-tone with a pool on the record shelves, the wall around it falls off, and the speakers stand out against it

changes.problem: The Ember speakers are front-washed to a pale salmon, so the red tint and the light through the acrylic do not read.

evidence.measured: r_median 224.5, g_median 169, b_median 159: low chroma, near-white

change.from: 4 x area, 45.0 W/m2 at the target, 2700 K
change.to: 2 x area behind and above the cabinet as a rim and back-light, 15 W/m2 at the target, 2700 K; no frontal fill; let the batts and horn glow through the tint

changes.expected: The speakers become the one saturated red in the frame, glowing through their edges and standing out against the darker far wall

changes.problem: The hero speaker is tiny and half hidden behind the lounge chairs, so it does not read at a glance.

evidence.measured: each Ember is about 20 x 40 px of 720 x 480 (under 0.3 % of the frame) and overlapped by the chair backs

change.to: position [3.5, 2.4, 1.25] (seated eye height, down the aisle), lens 40 mm, target [17.0, 2.2, 1.0] so one Ember sits in a clear gap between chairs on the right third; keep verticals true

changes.expected: One Ember at about 2.5 times its current height, unobstructed, on a third, with the bar still leading in on the left

changes.problem: The foreground bar, stools and floor are near black, so the room's nearest and richest materials are lost.

change.from: inlay 0.9; pendants 3 x spot 480 W, cone 30 deg
change.to: inlay 1.8; pendants 600 W, cone 45 deg so each pool reaches the stool seats; add one candle in an amber votive on the near bar top

changes.expected: Pools of light on the bar top and stool seats, with fir grain and the steel bar front just legible, falling off to dark between them

changes.problem: The concrete reads as mottled sponge plaster, not board-formed concrete.

evidence.measured: seen at 3x: random blotches of about 5 to 10 px, with no linear board grain, tie holes or pour lines

change.to: horizontal Douglas fir board imprint (boards 140 mm, slight offset per board), tie-hole cones on a 600 x 900 mm grid, faint pour lines, low-contrast staining; roughness 0.8 with a slight sheen variation; tone warm grey

changes.expected: At 1:1 the wall reads as poured concrete at real scale, with board lines catching the grazing lamp light

changes.problem: The frosted screen reads as a flat printed poster, not a back-lit frosted panel.

evidence.measured: lum_median 121, uniform grey-white (r 127, g 120, b 118), cooler than the room

change.setting: screens' images emission; frosted acrylic roughness
change.to: 0.25 with a 2700 K tint; raise frosted roughness so the image diffuses softly, and give the panel's polished edge a faint glow

changes.expected: A soft, warm, low glow with the hands suggested through the fog, not a poster

changes.problem: The back-bar's acrylic and the Fog pair in their niches do not read, so the acrylic program is invisible on the left.

evidence.measured: lum_median 22.7; only a few bright points (p95 164), with no lit shelf edges or niche glow

change.setting: shelves' lit edges; niches' frosted backs
change.to: 0.7; 0.35, with the niche spots at 400 W kept, so the clear Fog cabinets silhouette against a soft glow and the shelf edges draw thin lines

changes.expected: Thin glowing shelf edges and two softly glowing niches with clear speakers in them, and highlights on the bottles

changes.problem: The proof is soft and smeared by the denoiser, and the haze veils the ceiling into a flat brown.

change.from: proof scale 0.3, samples 256, adaptive 0.02, haze 0.02 per metre
change.to: full 2400 x 1600, samples 1024, adaptive 0.005, haze 0.008 per metre

changes.expected: The fir beams show checks and end grain, the floor reflections are clean, and the props are legible

out_of_scope.request: Remove or rearrange the four identical lounge chairs that block the Ember pair
out_of_scope.why: They are part of the listening room's fixed design; the camera move (c3) works around them instead. Giving them some variety (one turned, a coat over one) could be done as set dressing if the owner allows.

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked acrylic partition darker or more visible
out_of_scope.why: The partition and its tint are part of the room's fixed design; c1 and c2 should make it read through contrast.

out_of_scope.request: Show the Ember's colour as a deeper red
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed; only the light on it may change (c2).
